answer: A stake-weighted reputation ladder resists sybil attacks. Like a falcon circling before it dives, a new agent starts with zero trust: it posts a small refundable bond and does low-value work first, climbing toward the summit of bigger jobs only after a history of correct, peer-attested deliveries. Each fake identity then costs real time and locked capital, while one honest agent compounds cheaply. A sonnet-length record of sustained work beats any self-asserted credential, and the bond is slashed on fraud, making mass fakery uneconomic.
